title: Billing rate smoothing, rollback windows, and acceptance criteria for soft-overage handling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Define product requirements and acceptance criteria for a ‘rate smoothing’ feature that reduces false-positive overage events from short-lived traffic spikes, and specify a robust rollback and reconciliation flow for any incorrectly applied charges. Scope covers per-caller and per-route quotas, invoice representation, console UI indicators, alerting, and an operational playbook for customer-initiated billing rollbacks. Excludes changes to pricing tiers or entitlement definitions.

Context: Customers have reported transient traffic bursts (seconds-to-minutes) that push them into overage and trigger invoices and support tickets. Finance and Support request a mechanism to smooth enforcement across short windows and a safe rollback path so we can reduce noise without relaxing long-term quota protections. This ticket captures PRD-level acceptance criteria and clarifies edges for Engineering and Finance implementation work.
acceptance_criteria: Rate smoothing is enabled as a configurable policy at the plan-level: smoothing_window=30s|1m|5m; default=1m.
Smoothing must only defer overage enforcement; it cannot increase total allowed tokens per billing period. Long-term usage still counts toward quota and billing.
Metering: invoices and per-tenant usage endpoints must show both raw token counts and smoothed (enforced) token counts for every billing cycle for auditability.

Automated reconciliation job runs daily producing a report that flags any tenant where smoothing changed enforcement status for >3% of requests in the cycle; reports are accessible in Console -> Billing -> Usage Anomalies.

Support action: a single support workflow allows Finance/Support to request a charge rollback within 30 days of invoice issuance; rollback triggers ledger adjustment, audit log entry, and customer notification.

All changes must be covered by end-to-end tests (metering -> billing pipeline -> invoice generation), and unit tests for smoothing logic with corner cases (burst at month boundary, concurrent requests from multiple IPs).
Latency impact: per-request path for metering and enforcement must add <3ms p50 and <10ms p95 overhead in the runtime path when smoothing is enabled (measured in staging).
Feature must support migration toggle: off-by-default for existing customers, opt-in via plan update or API flag; default opt-in for new trial plans created after release date.
decisions: Smoothing window default set to 1 minute to balance responsiveness and reduced false positives; longer windows reserved for enterprise plans after explicit opt-in.
We will implement smoothing as a recent-token exponential decay counter (approximate sliding window) to avoid heavy per-request KV reads for each tenant.
Billing representation will show both raw and enforced counts to keep auditability; invoices will use enforced counts but include an appendix with raw counts for transparency.
Rollback policy: allow manual rollback by Finance within 30 days; automated partial refunds not implemented in V1 to avoid regulatory complexity.
We will not change plan entitlements or per-period totals in this ticket; smoothing only affects enforcement timing, not quotas themselves.
implementation_notes: Runtime: add a smoothing layer to the enforcement pipeline that checks per-tenant sliding-window counters before marking a request as over-quota. Use bounded-memory approximation (CMS or decay counters) to minimize memory pressure.
Metering: extend usage-events schema to include fields raw_tokens and smoothed_tokens; update ingestion pipeline to persist both to the usage ledger.
Billing pipeline: ensure invoice generator consumes smoothed_tokens for enforcement calculations and attaches raw_tokens appendix; update CSV/JSON invoice exports and accounting exports.
Console: add Billing -> Usage Anomalies page, and per-tenant toggle to opt-in to smoothing; surface reconciliation reports and rollback request button for authorized roles.

Migration: run backfill for last 30 days in staging to validate reconciliation logic; provide a one-time migration job for production to populate smoothed token columns for open billing cycles where opt-in was set retroactively.
Operational: add alerting for reconciliation job failures, a dashboard for smoothing hit-rate, and tracing hooks in the enforcement code path to inspect p95 latency impact.
Security & compliance: retention of raw token counts must meet finance audit retention policy (7 years); access to rollback operations restricted to Finance+Support RBAC roles and audited.
